Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

political adjective

also to do with politics, political science, for political reasons

classical

Cic. Inv. 1.6: cīvīlis scientia, political science (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 180
M-O s.v. political

cīvīlis, cīvīle

adjective, declension

political, to do with public life

Of public life as against private: officia cīvīlia (Quint. 2.15.36). A political career is cursus honōrum (Traupman 180).

Other words

  • dē rē pūblicā — about politics (of talk, views, writing)

    phrase: dē with the ablative · also used · classical · Cic. Rep. 1.12: dē rē pūblicā disputātiō (Lewis & Short)

    Much of what English calls political Latin says with rēs pūblica: talk dē rē pūblicā; for political reasons, reī pūblicae causā (Traupman 180); going into politics, ad rem pūblicam adīre (Cic. Rep. 1.12).

  • polīticus, polītica, polīticum — political, of political theory

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 3.109: philosophī polīticī (Lewis & Short); Cael. in Cic. Fam. 8.1.5: librī polīticī (Lewis & Short)

    Greek πολιτικός, used of political philosophers and of books on the state.

Examples

  • reī pūblicae causā
